The idea is simple: on this day, people are encouraged to greet at least ten others, showing the value of a personal connection as a step toward resolving contlicts and fostering understanding between individuals, countries, and cultures.

How it's observed:
• People greet at least ten other people-friends or strangers-in person, by phone, online, or by letter.
• Schools, leaders, and Nobel laureates have supported and participated in Worla Hello Day.
• The day is recognized and observed in over 180 countries.
Hello is a universal greeting. By saying hello, individuals emphasize that communication-rather than force-is essential to resolving disputes and building peace.
